summary: Fourth executed G3 review of EFMP-302 Unit 5, first look at the state repaired after run 003. The assessment bank was solved blind before any key or prior report was read; all ten derived MCQ answers agree with the published key. Four of the six run-002 findings the briefing described as carried were already closed by run 003 and are re-verified closed here; run002-f5-mcq-blueprint and run002-f9-status-comparison, the two that were genuinely still open, are both now repaired and verified. Three blocking findings remain or are newly opened: hennessy2022's unverifiable-source declaration still does not support the findings-level claims topic-03 draws from it; RRQ 9 sits below the approved blueprint's RRQ floor; and every ERQ rubric table on unit-assessment.mdx renders its top two bands off-screen at 360px with no horizontal scroll, which run 003 recorded as moot on a measurement of the table box rather than of its cells. Disposition is escalate rather than revise because the rubric-table defect is in the shared presentation layer and reproduces in every EFMP-302 unit including Unit 3, which has already published provisionally; because this is the fourth review cycle against a two-cycle limit; and because the bound manifest was hand-edited in the working tree rather than regenerated by `prepare`.

findings.message: Carried from run 003 as 'new-hennessy2022-declaration' (uncertain) and raised to blocking, because it is unrepaired and the rubric resolves it. specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-05.md line 41 declares hennessy2022 unretrievable with attempts, the date and the D-2026-0001 authorisation, but states the held evidence as 'the EdTech Hub companion record serves metadata only' and, unlike little2001 at line 40, states no level of support. docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-05/topic-03.mdx '### Pressure to integrate technology' then writes 'What it does establish is' and attributes three findings-level claims to it: that teacher development opportunities in such countries are limited and often not informed by research evidence, that technology offers real potential to extend both formal programmes and informal peer learning, and that outcomes so far are mixed. Metadata cannot establish any of the three, and there is no bound excerpt (specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/ holds no hennessy2022.md), so nothing in the bundle verifies them. The bundle also contradicts itself about what was read: specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md line 93 records 'Abstract read 2026-09-15' for this key. Per the G3 reference and D-2026-0001's stated limit, a declared-unretrievable source still fails `sources` where the prose states more than the declaration supports. Repair: state the support level in the line-41 declaration and reconcile it with content-spec.md line 93; if the basis is abstract-level, say so and the three claims stand as written, and add the uncorroborated marker to topic-03.mdx that topic-01.mdx already applies to its multilingual practices.

New this run; not raised by runs 001-003, which recorded only the mark weighting. The approved blueprint at specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md line 797 requires 'RRQs (10): Understand to Analyze'. unit-assessment.mdx '### Restricted-response questions (RRQs)' item 9, 'Name the three regions into which a teacher's situation divides, with two examples in each', is tagged (Remember), and the tag is honest: classified on the thinking actually required it is pure recall of three names and of examples given verbatim in topic-04.mdx '### Separating what is within a teacher's control from what is not'. It therefore sits below the floor this unit's blueprint sets. The deviation is unit-specific and deliberate elsewhere: Unit 3's blueprint at content-spec.md line 551 reads 'Remember to Analyze', so the Understand floor in Unit 5 is a choice, not boilerplate. The defect compounds with finding run002-f11, since this is also the most heavily weighted item in the bank. Repair: either raise the item to the floor (for example, ask what distinguishes the second region from the third and why the distinction matters), or amend the approved blueprint and record the amendment as a G1 decision.

Reopens run002-f18, which run 003 recorded as 'MOOT on this render'. Run 003 measured the <table> box (328px inside a 360px viewport) and the presence of 'Strong (4-5)' in the DOM; it did not measure the cells. Measured this run at 360x780 on a fresh build of 203d716: in ERQ rubric 1 the four columns occupy x=17-162, 162-276, 276-408 and 408-541, so 'Adequate (3)' is cut mid-word and the whole of 'Strong (4-5)' is off-screen. The wrapper computes overflow-x: visible with scrollWidth equal to clientWidth, and document.documentElement.scrollWidth is 360, so there is no horizontal scroll anywhere: the content is not merely unlabelled, it is unreachable. All five ERQ rubrics are affected (5 cells fully off-screen and 5 cut midway in rubrics 1-4; 5 cut midway in rubric 5). Evidence: logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u5-run007/table-geometry.log, logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u5-run007/table-clip-sweep.log, and renders-agent-g3-efmp302-u5-run007/narrow360-erq1-rubric-VIEWPORT.png, in which the Strong column is absent from the screen. What the learner loses is the descriptor that defines the top band of every extended-response rubric. The four two-column mini-rubrics in the topic files are unaffected (max cell right edge 344px), and A4 print is unaffected. Scope: this is the shared table presentation layer, not Unit 5 authoring - the same measurement reproduces on the unit-assessment page of EFMP-302 Units 2, 3, 4 and 6 (logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u5-run007/scope-probe.log), including Unit 3, which has already published provisionally. Repair belongs in the shared component or stylesheet, in the same place the figure carrier received role="region", tabindex="0" and an aria-label; it is not within this unit's authoring scope, which is part of why this report escalates.

Process finding about the handoff, not about the content. specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-05/G3-run007/manifest.json is modified in the working tree and not committed. The committed version (from 482eb52) binds the pre-repair digests of fig-U5-3.svg and fig-U5-3.dark.svg; the working-tree version binds the post-ded73ec digests. The skill directs a reviewer to verify digests against the prepared manifest and not to silently refresh it, and `prepare` refuses to run while a bound input is dirty, so this manifest cannot have come from `prepare` in its current state. I did not refresh it. I verified it instead: recomputing the bound set with the contract's own inputManifest(), including its translation_status normalisation, gives 137 paths matching 137, zero digest mismatches, zero paths added or dropped, and a matching skill_digest, and every bound content file is clean at HEAD 203d716. The binding is therefore truthful and reproducible, and the two edited digests are exactly those of the committed post-repair figure. What cannot be established from inside this session is that the bundle was produced by the trusted preparation path rather than by hand. Recorded as uncertain rather than blocking for that reason; it contributes to the escalate disposition and should be resolved by committing the reviewed state and regenerating the manifest with `prepare`.

Governance finding. The skill allows at most two repair/review cycles per stage per submission. Unit 5 at G3 already carries three executed reviews - agent-g3-efmp302-u5-run001 (escalate), run002 (escalate) and run003 (revise) - each followed by an authoring repair, and this is the fourth executed review. Input bundles were additionally prepared at G3-run004, -run005 and -run006 with no report written against them. The inputs have genuinely changed since run 003, so this is not a prohibited unchanged-input retry, and the remaining content defects are few and precisely located; but the cycle budget for this stage is spent, which is an escalation condition in its own right and which the owner should rule on before a fifth cycle is commissioned.
